title: As a final year graduate, what should be my daily preparation strategy for the UPSC IAS exam 2021?
reason: The user is asking for a daily preparation strategy as a beginner/final year student. The provided notes on syllabus-mapped reading, avoiding information overload, and structured daily targets are perfectly aligned with their needs.

matched_note.title: UPSC Daily Current Affairs & Editorial Analysis Strategy: The Hindu & Indian Express in 30 Minutes

drafted_comment:
The biggest mistake most graduates make is trying to read everything at once, which leads to burnout and information overload. You need a system, not just a schedule.

Here is how you should structure your daily routine:

1. Syllabus-Mapped Reading: Stop reading the newspaper like a news consumer. Read it through the lens of the GS syllabus. If a news item doesn't fit into a GS category (Society, Governance, Economy, etc.), skip it.
2. The 3-Pillar Rule: For every major issue you study, ensure you can note down three things: a Constitutional Article, a hard statistic, and a specific Committee recommendation (like NITI Aayog or 2nd ARC). This turns passive reading into Mains-ready content.
3. Consistency over Intensity: Focus on 4 hours of high-quality, syllabus-targeted study daily rather than 10 hours of aimless reading.\n
